input.instructions: Create a compact, accurate blueprint for an 8-to-12-minute educational lesson with exactly ten sequential teaching beats. Do not write full narration. Create exactly three measurable learning objectives. For every beat, provide one distinct complete factual claim, a concrete example, a concise editable visual direction, and one or two exact supplied source IDs. End the claim, example, and visual direction with complete punctuation. Every cited source excerpt must directly support the claim; reuse at least two important technical terms from each cited excerpt so support can be checked locally. Do not invent course assignments, policies, measurements, datasets, instruction encodings, or product behavior that is absent from the supplied excerpts. Keep the claim, example, and visual direction compact; a deterministic local expander will produce the full narration. Sequence the beats from foundations through application and end with a practical analysis checklist. Use only the supplied source excerpts for factual claims. Every factual claim must cite one or more supplied source IDs. Narration must describe information that is essential to understand visuals. Do not imitate a named creator or invent sources.
input.prompt:
Topic: CSCI-140: Computer Science for AP Students. Create a representative course-foundations companion aligned to the official catalog description. It must teach durable concepts and problem-solving methods without claiming to replace the instructor's syllabus. Official catalog description: This accelerated course covers material from the first-year sequence of courses and provides the foundation for all subsequent Computer Science courses. The course stresses problem solving while covering modern software development techniques and introducing essential software tools. Topics include tree and graph structures, nested data structures, objects, classes, inheritance, interfaces, object-oriented collection class libraries for abstract data types (e.g. stacks, queues, maps, and trees), and static vs. dynamic data types. Concepts of object- oriented design are a large part of the course. Software qualities related to object orientation, namely cohesion, minimal coupling, modifiability, and extensibility, are all introduced in this course, as well as a few elementary object-oriented design patterns. Input and output streams, graphical user interfaces, and exception handling are covered. Note: Requires department permission for registration. Contact Hours: Lecture/Lab 6 It may be used to fulfill one of the following: GE: Elective, GE: Mathematical Perspective, NTID Math Processes, SMTL: Science/Math Literacy Typically Offered: Fall

Source excerpts:

[llvm-language-reference]
LLVM IR is a typed, SSA-based intermediate representation with explicit instructions, basic blocks, functions, memory operations, and control flow. A module contains global values, functions, declarations, and metadata. A function contains basic blocks, and every basic block ends with a terminator instruction. Phi instructions select values according to the predecessor control-flow edge. Load and store instructions make memory access explicit. Valid IR must satisfy structural and typing rules. The verifier reports IR that violates those rules. Compiler work separates parsing and semantic analysis from lowering, verification, optimization, and target-specific code generation.

[python-language-reference]
The Python language reference specifies lexical analysis, data model behavior, execution, expressions, statements, functions, classes, exceptions, and module import semantics. Python objects have identity, a type, and a value. Names are bound to objects within namespaces and scopes. Expressions produce values, while statements control execution and bindings. Exceptions interrupt normal control flow until a matching handler processes them or they propagate. The import system searches for modules and binds loaded modules into a namespace. Programs should be reasoned about through explicit state, control flow, data representation, contracts, tests, and observable behavior. Debugging separates syntax, runtime, and logical failures, while decomposition and abstraction reduce the number of interacting concerns.

Concepts of object- oriented design are a large part of the course. Software qualities related to object orientation, namely cohesion, minimal coupling, modifiability, and extensibility, are all introduced in this course, as well as a few elementary object-oriented design patterns. Input and output streams, graphical user interfaces, and exception handling are covered. Note: Requires department permission for registration. beats.claim: CSCI-140 provides the foundation for all subsequent Computer Science courses by covering first-year sequence material and stressing problem solving.
beats.example: Students will use this course to prepare for advanced topics like algorithms, data structures, and software engineering.
beats.title: Course Foundations & Scope
beats.visualDirection: Display a course roadmap graphic showing CSCI-140 as the central hub connecting to advanced CS courses.

beats.claim: Static and dynamic data types are fundamental concepts in modern software development, determining when type checking occurs.
beats.example: In statically typed languages, variable types are checked at compile time, whereas dynamically typed languages check types at runtime.
beats.title: Static vs. Dynamic Data Types
beats.visualDirection: Show a side-by-side comparison table of static vs. dynamic typing with code snippets highlighting compile-time vs. runtime type resolution.

beats.claim: Object-oriented design relies on objects, classes, inheritance, and interfaces to structure software effectively.
beats.example: A parent class defines shared behavior, while child classes inherit and extend that behavior through polymorphism.
beats.title: Object-Oriented Design Foundations
beats.visualDirection: Render a class diagram illustrating inheritance relationships between a base class and derived classes.

beats.claim: Object-oriented collection class libraries provide abstract data types like stacks, queues, maps, and trees for efficient data management.
beats.example: A stack implements last-in-first-out behavior, while a queue implements first-in-first-out behavior for ordered data processing.
beats.title: Abstract Data Types & Collections
beats.visualDirection: Animate a stack and queue data structure showing push/pop and enqueue/dequeue operations with labeled elements.

beats.claim: Software quality in object-oriented design is measured by cohesion and minimal coupling to ensure maintainable code.
beats.example: High cohesion means a class performs a single, well-defined purpose, while minimal coupling reduces dependencies between classes.
beats.title: Software Qualities: Cohesion & Minimal Coupling
beats.visualDirection: Display a before-and-after class diagram showing how refactoring improves cohesion and reduces coupling.

beats.claim: Exception handling interrupts normal control flow until a matching handler processes the error or it propagates.
beats.example: A try-catch block catches a runtime error, allowing the program to recover or exit gracefully without crashing.
beats.title: Exception Handling & Control Flow
beats.visualDirection: Show a control flow diagram with a normal path and an exception path branching to a handler block.

beats.claim: Compiler work separates parsing and semantic analysis from lowering, verification, optimization, and target-specific code generation.
beats.example: LLVM IR serves as a typed, SSA-based intermediate representation that enables cross-platform optimization and code generation.
beats.title: Compiler & IR Concepts
beats.visualDirection: Illustrate a compiler pipeline diagram with stages: parsing, semantic analysis, lowering, verification, optimization, code generation.

beats.claim: Python objects have identity, a type, and a value, and programs should be reasoned about through explicit state, control flow, and contracts.
beats.example: Debugging separates syntax, runtime, and logical failures, while decomposition and abstraction reduce interacting concerns in Python code.
beats.title: Python Language Model & Execution
beats.visualDirection: Show a Python object model diagram with identity, type, and value attributes, alongside a debugging workflow flowchart.

beats.claim: Elementary object-oriented design patterns are introduced to improve software structure and reusability.
beats.example: The singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance, while the factory pattern creates objects without specifying exact classes.
beats.title: Object-Oriented Design Patterns
beats.visualDirection: Display a simple UML diagram of a factory pattern with creator, product, and concrete product classes.

beats.claim: Students must verify that software designs meet cohesion, minimal coupling, modifiability, and extensibility standards.
beats.example: A checklist evaluates whether each class has a single responsibility, limited dependencies, and clear extension points for future features.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: Show a printable checklist template with checkboxes for cohesion, coupling, modifiability, and extensibility evaluation.

learningObjectives: Define and distinguish between static and dynamic data types using language reference specifications.
Explain how objects, classes, and inheritance form the foundation of object-oriented design.
Apply cohesion and minimal coupling principles to evaluate software quality in object-oriented structures.
